description:
2020 Decennial Census counts for all **8,174,955** census blocks in the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico — the smallest geography the Census Bureau publishes anything for. From the [2020 Census P.L. 94-171 Redistricting Data Summary Files](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/about/rdo/summary-files.html): total population and the seven race-alone counts plus two or more races ([P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1)), Hispanic or Latino and White-alone-not-Hispanic ([P2](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P2)), the voting-age population 18 and over ([P3](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P3)), housing units occupied and vacant ([H1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.H1)), and the group-quarters population ([P5](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P5)), with derived shares and population density.

These are **complete counts, not survey estimates**, so there are no margins of error and no coefficients of variation — the `*_moe` and `*_cv` columns the ACS collections carry do not exist here. They are, however, protected by the 2020 disclosure-avoidance system, which injects noise at block level while holding state totals exact: block counts are reliable in aggregate and should be read with care one block at a time. The Census Bureau publishes no income, education or commuting data at block level — for that, move up to the [block-group collections](../block-groups/catalog.json).

Roughly three in ten census blocks are unpopulated by design (28.97% have `pop_total = 0`, measured), so `pct_white_nh`, `pct_black` and `pct_hispanic` are NULL on that share of rows, and `pct_vacant` is NULL on the 27.64% with no housing units. That is a property of census blocks, not missing data: filter `pop_total > 0` before averaging a rate. Summed over the 50 states and DC, `pop_total` equals 331,449,281 — the published 2020 resident population, exactly; Puerto Rico equals 3,285,874.

Geometry is [TIGER/Line 2024 `TABBLOCK20`](https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2024/TABBLOCK20/), not the cartographic boundary files the ACS collections use, because no cartographic edition is published for blocks. TIGER is unclipped, so a coastal block extends to the 3-mile limit rather than the shoreline, and `aland_sqkm` comes from the file's own `ALAND20` land-area field (water-only blocks have `ALAND20 = 0` and so a NULL `pop_density`). Field positions in the P.L. 94-171 files are pinned against the Census Bureau's own [R import scripts](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial/rdo/about/2020-census-program/Phase3/SupportMaterials/2020PL_R_import_scripts.zip) rather than read off a PDF — see the build notes in the repository for the field table and the three independent checks behind it.

The collection is **hive-partitioned by state**: 52 parquet files under `state_fips=<FIPS>/`, one STAC item each with its own bbox and row count. Pull one state and you download one file. To query all 52 as one table use the glob over the anonymous S3 endpoint (`SET s3_region='us-west-2'; ... read_parquet('s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog/blocks/state_fips=*/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=true)`) — an HTTPS glob cannot list a directory and returns 404; see the [agent guide](AGENTS.md) for the tested forms. The synthesized `state_fips` key carries the numeric FIPS code and sits alongside the `state` column's USPS code.

The PMTiles archive is a census-geography pyramid built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo): z0–z5 are county polygons and z6–z9 census tracts carrying exact sums of the 2020 block counts — decennial counts aggregate exactly, and the rate columns are recomputed from the summed counts rather than averaged — and z10–z14 are the blocks themselves. Thinning 8.1 million polygons down to a national zoom would show a biased subset (small urban blocks drop first) rather than less data, so the coarse zooms step up to a coarser census geography instead. Every band carries the same column names, so one style expression classifies every zoom — but below z10 you are looking at counties and tracts, not blocks, and clicking a coarse feature identifies a real county or tract by `geoid` and `name`. Statistics come from the GeoParquet, never from the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

styles/black-share.title: Black share
styles/black-share.description: Share of residents who are Black or African American alone, pale to deep green. Measured over all 5,806,512 blocks with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 1%/5%/15%/35%/65%, which fall at the 59th/70th/82nd/91st/95th percentile of the national distribution. 28.97% have no published value and draw in neutral gray rather than as a low value.

styles/default.title: Population density
styles/default.description: People per square kilometre of land area on roughly logarithmic steps, pale cream to deep plum; the lowest class is almost entirely the blocks with no residents at all. Measured over all 7,936,543 blocks with a published value: 7 classes with breaks at 1/10/50/200/800/2,500 people per km², which fall at the 28th/35th/44th/51st/63rd/84th percentile of the national distribution.

styles/hispanic-share.title: Hispanic or Latino share
styles/hispanic-share.description: Share of residents who are Hispanic or Latino of any race, pale apricot to burnt orange. Measured over all 5,806,512 blocks with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 2%/6%/15%/30%/60%, which fall at the 40th/51st/68th/82nd/92nd percentile of the national distribution. 28.97% have no published value and draw in neutral gray rather than as a low value.

styles/vacancy.title: Vacant housing units
styles/vacancy.description: Share of housing units vacant on Census Day 2020, cream to dark red; blocks with no housing units draw as no data, not as zero. Measured over all 5,915,599 blocks with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 5%/15%/30%/50%/75%, which fall at the 69th/77th/83rd/87th/91st percentile of the national distribution. 27.64% have no published value and draw in neutral gray rather than as a low value.

styles/white-share.title: White, non-Hispanic share
styles/white-share.description: Share of residents who are white alone and not Hispanic or Latino, pale to deep blue. Measured over all 5,806,512 blocks with a published value: 7 classes with breaks at 10%/30%/50%/70%/85%/95%, which fall at the 12th/20th/30th/47th/65th/80th percentile of the national distribution. 28.97% have no published value and draw in neutral gray rather than as a low value.

source-pl94171.title: 2020 Census P.L. 94-171 Redistricting Data Summary Files — state directories
source-pl94171.description: The 52 state archives (`{State_Name}/{ab}2020.pl.zip`) this collection's counts were read from, 2020 Census P.L. 94-171 redistricting data. Each archive holds a pipe-delimited geoheader plus three segment files joined on `LOGRECNO`; block records are `SUMLEV = '750'`. Served by census.gov.

source-tiger-tabblock20.title: TIGER/Line 2024 TABBLOCK20 — 2020 census block shapefiles by state
source-tiger-tabblock20.description: The block geometry: `tl_2024_{fips}_tabblock20.zip` per state, from which only `GEOID20` and `ALAND20` are kept. Unclipped, EPSG:4269 upstream, reprojected to EPSG:4326 with ogr2ogr. Served by census.gov.

source-pl-import-scripts.title: 2020 P.L. 94-171 R import scripts (field layout)
source-pl-import-scripts.description: The Census Bureau's own machine-readable field dictionary for the P.L. 94-171 files. Every field position this build reads is pinned against the `colnames()` assignments in `R Versions/pl_part{1,2,3}_2020_dar.r` and `pl_geohd_2020_dar.r` — the citable layout source, rather than the technical-documentation PDF. Downloaded 2026-11-12.

doc-pl94171-techdoc.title: 2020 Census P.L. 94-171 Redistricting Data Summary File — technical documentation
doc-pl94171-techdoc.description: Table shells, universes, file layout and the disclosure-avoidance description for the 2020 redistricting files.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 15-character 2020 census block GEOID — state (2) + county (3) + tract (6) + block (4), e.g. `020130001001000`. The geoheader's `GEOCODE` field, not its `GEOID` (which carries a `7500000US` summary-level prefix); the build asserts `GEOCODE == STATE || COUNTY || TRACT || BLOCK` on every row. `substr(geoid, 1, 12)` is the block group, so blocks join the ACS block-group collections by prefix.

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do. In the block collection this sits alongside the hive partition key `state_fips`, which carries the numeric FIPS code.

table:columns.name: pop_total
table:columns.description: Total population of the block, from the 2020 Decennial Census. Universe: total population. Table P1, cell 1 (`P0010001`) of [P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1). Read from the 2020 P.L. 94-171 redistricting file at the field position pinned in `docs/blocks-build-notes.md` against the Census Bureau's own R import scripts. A complete count, not a survey estimate, so there is no margin of error — but it is protected by the 2020 disclosure-avoidance system, which injects noise at the block level and exact-counts states. Blocks tile their state exhaustively: summed over the 50 states and DC this column equals 331,449,281, the published 2020 resident population, exactly. 28.97% of all 8,174,955 blocks have a population of 0 (measured).

table:columns.name: pop_white
table:columns.description: Population reporting White alone. Universe: total population. Table P1, cell 3 (`P0010003`) of [P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1) — a race-alone count, crossing Hispanic origin, so it is not comparable to `pop_white_nh`.

table:columns.name: pop_black
table:columns.description: Population reporting Black or African American alone. Universe: total population. Table P1, cell 4 (`P0010004`) of [P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1). Race alone, crossing Hispanic origin.

table:columns.name: pop_aian
table:columns.description: Population reporting American Indian and Alaska Native alone. Universe: total population. Table P1, cell 5 (`P0010005`) of [P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1).

table:columns.name: pop_asian
table:columns.description: Population reporting Asian alone. Universe: total population. Table P1, cell 6 (`P0010006`) of [P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1).

table:columns.name: pop_nhpi
table:columns.description: Population reporting Native Hawaiian and Other Pacific Islander alone. Universe: total population. Table P1, cell 7 (`P0010007`) of [P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1).

table:columns.name: pop_other
table:columns.description: Population reporting Some Other Race alone. Universe: total population. Table P1, cell 8 (`P0010008`) of [P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1).

table:columns.name: pop_two_plus
table:columns.description: Population reporting two or more races. Universe: total population. Table P1, cell 9 (`P0010009`) of [P1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P1). The seven race-alone columns plus this one sum exactly to `pop_total`; P1's cell 2 ("Population of one race") is an intermediate subtotal and is deliberately not carried, which is why the sum closes.

table:columns.name: pop_hispanic
table:columns.description: Population of Hispanic or Latino origin, of any race. Universe: total population. Table P2, cell 2 (`P0020002`) of [P2](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P2). Hispanic origin is asked separately from race, so this crosses all seven race columns.

table:columns.name: pop_white_nh
table:columns.description: Population reporting White alone and not Hispanic or Latino. Universe: total population. Table P2, cell 5 (`P0020005`) of [P2](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P2) — the not-Hispanic branch, so this is a subset of `pop_white` and the two are not interchangeable.

table:columns.name: vap_total
table:columns.description: Voting-age population: people 18 years and over. Universe: population 18 years and over. Table P3, cell 1 (`P0030001`) of [P3](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P3). The table this column comes from is the one P.L. 94-171 exists to publish — the race detail behind redistricting — and `pop_total − vap_total` is the under-18 population.

table:columns.name: housing_units
table:columns.description: Total housing units in the block, occupied and vacant. Universe: housing units. Table H1, cell 1 (`H0010001`) of [H1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.H1). A complete count of units, not of households.

table:columns.name: housing_occupied
table:columns.description: Occupied housing units. Universe: housing units. Table H1, cell 2 (`H0010002`) of [H1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.H1). `housing_occupied + housing_vacant == housing_units` holds on every block in this collection; the build checks it (0 violations).

table:columns.name: housing_vacant
table:columns.description: Vacant housing units. Universe: housing units. Table H1, cell 3 (`H0010003`) of [H1](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.H1). Includes seasonal, for-rent and for-sale units, so it is not a measure of abandonment.

table:columns.name: group_quarters_pop
table:columns.description: Population living in group quarters — correctional facilities, juvenile facilities, nursing facilities, college/university housing, military quarters, other group quarters. Universe: population in group quarters. Table P5, cell 1 (`P0050001`) of [P5](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALPL2020.P5). Group-quarters residents are included in `pop_total` but live in no housing unit, which is how a block can hold hundreds of people and few or no units.

table:columns.name: pct_white_nh
table:columns.description: `pop_white_nh` as a percent of `pop_total`, 2 decimals. Universe: total population. NULL where `pop_total` is 0 — 28.97% of blocks (measured), because roughly three in ten census blocks are unpopulated by design. That is a property of census blocks, not missing data: filter `pop_total > 0` before averaging.

table:columns.name: pct_black
table:columns.description: `pop_black` as a percent of `pop_total`, 2 decimals. Universe: total population — and note the numerator is race-alone, crossing Hispanic origin, unlike the ACS collections' `pct_black`. NULL where `pop_total` is 0 (28.97% of blocks, measured).

table:columns.name: pct_hispanic
table:columns.description: `pop_hispanic` as a percent of `pop_total`, 2 decimals. Universe: total population. NULL where `pop_total` is 0 (28.97% of blocks, measured).

table:columns.name: pct_vacant
table:columns.description: `housing_vacant` as a percent of `housing_units`, 2 decimals. Universe: housing units. NULL where the block has no housing units — 27.64% of blocks (measured).

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `pop_total / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND20` is 0 — a water-only block has no land to divide by; 2.92% of the 8,174,955 blocks are NULL on this column (measured).

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND20 / 1e6` from the TIGER/Line 2024 block file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. TIGER/Line 2024 `TABBLOCK20`, which is **not** shoreline-clipped: a coastal block extends to the 3-mile limit. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.

table:columns.name: state_fips
table:columns.description: Hive partition key, synthesized from the directory name when the `state_fips=*/*.parquet` glob is read — the 2-digit state FIPS code of the partition. Not a column in the parquet files themselves. Named `state_fips` rather than `state` so it does not shadow the USPS `state` column.
